observations.comment: Things the design says that look like mistakes. Reproduced exactly rather than reconciled — choosing otherwise would be inventing content or a decision.
observations.threeIdenticalCards: 16157:21831, 17693:12607 and 17693:12626 carry the SAME title, person, tag, surface and stepper. Three identical rows reads as unfinished work in Figma rather than a design decision, but giving each a different title would be inventing content.
observations.stageCardSignals: Each card is a THEME surface with an IN PROGRESS stepper and a green COMPLETE tag — three signals, three states. Same disagreement as 14632:8829.
observations.buttonCaseAcrossFrames: This frame's button is sentence case; the Button instance on 14632:8829 renders CLOSE CASE. The file is inconsistent about button case between frames.

frame_comment: Machine-readable geometry, read by scripts/verify-frame.mjs. Every value is from the saved extract. These frames are NOT the People First Card — the header and subject are plain Figma frames, and the stage card is `Clickable card` from a non-People-First library (F-018) — so they are built in local CSS and asserted here rather than merely declared.

divergences.components: Stepper, People, Rectangle Tags and Right arrow come from a non-People-First library (F-018).
divergences.tags: Figma uses Rectangle Tags with alpha fills. The prototype uses the People First Tags component.
divergences.personName12px: 12px is not on the People First type ramp; the prototype uses the 13px label class with a declared `accept`.
divergences.buttonWeight: Figma draws Close case 13px Regular; .pf-button is 13px SemiBold. Case matches on this frame, so weight is the only difference.
